label: FICTION. Written to exercise the prioritization calculator.
note: These eleven recommendations, their estimates and the finding IDs they cite are invented. They are internally consistent with the synthetic evidence register in ../../uiowa_rfq_18649_workshare/methodology/23-synthetic-evidence-register.csv so the two fixtures can be read together, but nothing here describes the University of Iowa, any real system, or any real assessment. No estimate below was supplied by anyone at the University.

scales.effects: 0-5. 0 means ASSESSED AND EXPECTED TO HAVE NO EFFECT. It is a real estimate.
scales.complexity: 1-5. There is no 0: 'no effort' is not a real estimate.
scales.missing: Omit the field, or set it to null or "UNKNOWN". It stays UNKNOWN and is never read as 0.

recommendations.title: Reconcile production deployment approvals with the written two-approval procedure

quality.basis: Fictional: removes the ambiguity about which approval path a change actually took

security.basis: Fictional: approval on privileged deployments is the control the conflicting evidence is about

delivery.basis: Fictional: a documented exception path is faster than the current case-by-case handling

complexity.basis: Fictional: procedure text plus a change-record field; no platform work

recommendations.notes: Cites the synthetic register's conflict group CG-SYN-IAM-DEP-01 (procedure requires two approvals; seven of twelve sampled changes record one).

recommendations.title: Extend the required build-and-test status check to the remaining ESS repositories

quality.basis: Fictional: the check is the single largest defect filter in the fictional ESS pipeline

security.basis: Fictional: catches some dependency problems, but is not a security control

complexity.basis: Fictional: repository settings plus a short migration window per repository

recommendations.notes: The strength case: well estimated on every dimension, and stable near the top under most weightings.

recommendations.title: Re-run the privileged-access review and record the result against the published standard

quality.basis: Fictional: small effect; this is an assurance activity, not a build activity

security.basis: Fictional: the standard requires an annual review and no current record exists

delivery.basis: ASSESSED: no expected delivery effect. The review runs outside the release path. This is a real estimate of zero, not a missing one.

complexity.basis: Fictional: one reviewer, one reporting cycle

recommendations.notes: Carries a deliberate real 0 so the worksheet can be checked for treating 0 and UNKNOWN as the same thing. They are not.

recommendations.title: Generate ESS release notes from the change records instead of by hand

quality.basis: Fictional: fewer omissions in the notes themselves

security.basis: ASSESSED: no expected security effect. Release notes are a communication artifact. Real estimate of zero.

delivery.basis: Fictional: removes a manual step from every release

complexity.basis: Fictional: a template plus a report against existing change data

recommendations.notes: Under a security-only weighting this scores exactly 0.0 and is still ranked. A real zero is a result; a missing estimate is not.

recommendations.title: Consolidate the three group-membership review spreadsheets into one recorded quarterly review

quality.basis: Fictional: one source removes the reconciliation step between three sheets

security.basis: Fictional: makes an unreviewed group visible instead of falling between sheets

delivery.basis: Fictional: minor; this work sits outside delivery

complexity.basis: Fictional: three owners have to agree on one format before anything is merged

recommendations.title: Write down the RIS branch and review conventions that are currently held by convention

security.basis: Fictional: makes the review expectation checkable

delivery.basis: Fictional: less rework from mismatched expectations

complexity.basis: Fictional: writing is cheap; agreement across the group is not

recommendations.notes: Half of the deliberate tie: benefit 3.00 at the baseline weighting from an even 3/3/3 spread.

recommendations.title: Move the ESS shared service account off a static credential

quality.basis: ASSESSED: no expected quality effect on the software itself. Real estimate of zero.

security.basis: Fictional: removes a long-lived shared credential

delivery.basis: Fictional: also removes the quarterly manual rotation from the release checklist

complexity.basis: Fictional: every consumer of the account has to be found and cut over

recommendations.notes: The other half of the deliberate tie: benefit 3.00 from a completely different 0/5/4 spread. Same score, different reasons; the tie report shows both.

recommendations.title: Replace the manual IAM connector release checklist with a scripted release

quality.basis: Fictional: the checklist is where the fictional step-skips happen

security.basis: Fictional: a scripted release leaves a record the manual one does not

delivery.basis: Fictional: the checklist is the longest manual step in the fictional IAM release

recommendations.notes: THE GAP. Complexity was never estimated: whether the vendor connector supports a scripted release is itself unknown, and the answer moves the effort between a day and a quarter. Effects are strong, so this item's upper bound reaches the top of the list. It is held out of the ranking, NOT scored 0 and NOT ranked last.

recommendations.title: Document the RIS maintenance-window handoff between the on-call and platform rotations
recommendations.notes: A second gap, of a different kind. The security effect was never estimated, so this is unranked too, but its best possible score still does not reach the top of the list: the missing estimate is real and is still not what is holding up the decision.

recommendations.title: Inventory where the ESS group already uses assistive code generation

quality.basis: Not estimated. Whether assistive generation currently helps or hurts ESS code quality is exactly what the inventory is meant to find out, so entering a number here would be inventing the answer.

security.basis: Fictional: knowing where it is used is a precondition for any review of it

delivery.basis: Fictional: the inventory is short and unblocks the other AI-readiness work

complexity.basis: Fictional: a survey and a repository scan

recommendations.notes: Demonstrates weight-dependent materiality: unranked under any weighting that values quality, ranked under the security-only stress weighting where the missing quality estimate cannot change the order. The estimate is reported as missing in both cases.

recommendations.title: Define an approval path for AI-assisted changes to IAM configuration
recommendations.notes: Deliberately carries no finding_ids. It ranks normally but is reported as not traceable to a finding, which is a gap in the recommendation, not in the arithmetic.
